item.title: Newscast – Wednesday, Feb. 11, 2026
item.description: In this newscast: The Juneau School District is returning over $1 million earmarked for child care back to the city; The Alaska Department of Transportation has faced intense scrutiny in recent months over its plan to build a new ferry terminal between Juneau and Haines. item.title: Alaska’s chief justice highlights progress on court delays in speech to Legislature
item.description: Alaska Supreme Court Chief Justice Susan Carney highlighted efforts to reduce case backlogs and asked lawmakers to fund a new judge and courthouse maintenance.

item.title: ‘Acoustic Turbulence’ from Orpheus Project combines music, poetry and movement to explore life’s journey
item.description: Juneau Afternoon featuring new original work "Acoustic Turbulence" from Orpheus Project, Underwater Archeologist Kelly Monteleone's Fireside talk, and Juneau Audubon shares "Fins, Furs, and Feathers of the Amazon and Galapagos."

item.title: Q&A with Juneau’s Alaska Fellows Program VOAD coordinator on improving local disaster response
item.description: Akanksha Basil is tasked with improving the community's disaster response.

item.title: Alaska lawmakers grill transportation officials over controversial ferry project
item.description: The pushback has largely centered around concerns that the new terminal would make regional travel less convenient and efficient, not more, as the state has argued.

item.title: Alaska lawmakers float sending inmates out of state as prison costs mount
item.description: Faced with rising costs in the Department of Corrections, some lawmakers say it's an uncomfortable choice they may be forced to make.

item.title: Alaska Marine Lines, ferry system staff discuss options for safely transporting electric vehicles to Southeast Alaska
item.description: AML still won’t ship EVs while the Alaska Marine Highway System says it has improved safety procedures.

item.title: Three men were detained and removed from Juneau by immigration enforcement last year
item.description: The Juneau Police Department says its knowledge of these incidents and its involvement with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement activity in Juneau is very limited.

item.title: Tlingit & Haida seeks cultural ambassadors for summer 2026, Wearable Art goes ‘CAMP!,’ and Spice Juneau preps to celebrate Holi
item.description: Juneau Afternoon featuring Tlingit & Haida's Cultural Ambassador Program, Nimmy from Spice previews upcoming community events, including the next Holi Celebration, and Wearable Art goes CAMP!
